title: Perturbation-efficient Zeroth-order Optimization for Hardware-friendly On-device Training
problem: Zeroth-order optimization for neural network training generates excessive random numbers, making it infeasible for FPGAs and ASICs. Memory and resource constraints prevent efficient hardware implementation.
method: PeZO framework using random number reuse strategies and hardware-friendly adaptive scaling to replace Gaussian with uniform distribution, reducing resource consumption.
key_novelty: First to explore on-device zeroth-order optimization with perturbation-efficient random number generation strategy.
contributions: Identifies hardware-algorithm mismatch in random number generation for ZO optimization
Achieves 48.6% LUT and 12.7% FF reduction with up to 86% power savings
